history.recommendation_text: The Board recommends that the Administration provide training to staff members responsible to ensure the proper recording of fuel data, and regularly monitor and analyse fuel consumption to identify and investigate irregular fuel consumption.
history.administration_response: The Administration stated that, in its efforts to implement the recommendation, the Administration has conducted the following activities: (1) When the electronic fuel management system is deployed in a mission, onsite “train the trainers” sessions are part of the deployment process; (2) trainers/electronic fuel management system focal points who have received the “train the trainers” training are responsible to produce the training to other mission staff members. Mission focal points for the electronic fuel management system are in daily contact with the Office of Information and Communication Technology for any kind of support on the system and, in some cases, missions have requested ad hoc training to the Office on the system; (3) To further enhance Headquarters support to missions, Office of Supply Chain Management/Department of Operational Support has developed online training on fuel, including a specific module on fuel theft, which is available to all United Nations staff with a United Nations account (the training portal is available at https://unitednations.sharepoint.com/sit es/COP-Fuel_Community-DOS); (4) the Office of Supply Chain Management/Logistics Division has planned to organize one-time refresher training on fuel consumption analysis addressed to all electronic fuel management system trainers. Training will be divided in various sessions along the fourth quarter of 2022 and the first quarter of 2023. Recorded sessions will be uploaded in the fuel community of practice at the disposal of the missions for further training of staff. In view of the above, the Administration considers the recommendation as implemented.
history.board_assessment: The Board notes that the administration has organized training in the field. The Board considers this recommendation as implemented.
